reference.ceilingWording: a full-project archive on the program's reference dataset must cost CIVOS <= AUD 12.00 ex-GST all-in for one generation plus three downloads within the retention window
reference.unitNote: Cost arithmetic uses DECIMAL GB because that is the unit both vendors bill in. The §4.5.3 cap formula uses BINARY GiB as the spec directs. The two are kept separate and converted explicitly, never conflated.

railwayEgressPerGb.quote: Network egress (outbound data transfer) is charged at $0.05/GB.

railwayUploadCountsAsEgress.quote: Note that service egress is not free. If your service sends data to users or uploads files to a bucket, that traffic counts as service egress.

railwayIngressPerGb.notPublished: Railway publishes no ingress rate and no "ingress is free" statement; the billable-resource list is vCPU, memory, volumes and network egress only. Modelled at 0 with that assumption stated, not asserted as free.

supabaseEgressUncachedPerGb.quote: $0.09 per GB per month for uncached egress, $0.03 per GB per month for cached egress

supabaseIngressPerGb.notPublished: Supabase publishes no ingress/upload charge and no explicit "ingress is free" statement. Modelled at 0 with that assumption stated.

audPerUsd.note: ECB-derived reference rate. 2026-07-28 close; no 2026-07-29 rate was published at the time of reading. Cross-checked against https://tradingeconomics.com/australia/currency (0.6968).

standardUpload.quote: Though you can upload up to 5GB files using the standard upload method, we recommend using TUS Resumable Upload for uploading files greater than 6MB in size for better reliability.

resumableAndS3.quote: On the Pro Plan and up, you can set this value to up to 500 GB.
resumableAndS3.correctsSpec: Spec §4.5.3 says 'TUS/S3 paths reach 50 GB'. That is OUT OF DATE. Supabase raised the ceiling to 500 GB (https://supabase.com/blog/storage-500gb-uploads-cheaper-egress-pricing, 2025-07-18: 'Increasing the maximum file size to 500 GB, up from 50 GB') and the s3-uploads guide now states 500 GB. The 50 GB figure survives only on a stale troubleshooting page (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/troubleshooting/upload-file-size-restrictions-Y4wQLT), which contradicts both. The upload-protocol limb of the cap formula is therefore NOT the binding constraint it was assumed to be.
resumableAndS3.isPlanSetting: It is a configurable global Storage setting capped by plan, not a hard product limit — Free 50 MB, Pro/Team 500 GB, Enterprise custom, and above 500 GB requires contacting Supabase.

generationOnlyFloor.meaning: Read + upload + storage, ZERO downloads, on the spec-compliant path. This is the irreducible cost of producing the artefact at all.

verdict.theThreeFixes: §4.5.6 names three, all Jay decisions: (1) a lower cap, (2) a cheaper delivery path, (3) a priced add-on. This script reports which the numbers point at. It does not choose.
